precepts.text: A wise man is strong; yea, a man of knowledge increaseth strength. Fasting alone drops weight the body will store back; you have to exercise, and you are not getting younger.
precepts.point: A pastor challenged the captain saying he eats people like him for dinner, so the captain took him to gluttony with thirty scriptures on the church page. Health is a doctrine too.

note.label: Prepare Ye War

precepts.why:
“What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?” So you have to prepare ye war physically. This is war. Strengthen your body and keep it under control; you are not your own.

“A wise man is strong; yea, a man of knowledge increaseth strength.” A wise man is strong, and some of you brothers cannot do ten push-ups. Brothers get upset because the camp sets weight standards, and they can't run worth a damn thing; they cannot run three, four, five miles. Sisters, get in shape too. How the hell are you going to go out and teach when you are unfit?

A pastor once challenged the captain, fat as hell, saying he eats people like him up for dinner. Since he started with dinner, the answer was gluttony: about thirty scriptures of correction on his own church page. Not a debate about the color of Christ first; deal with your health right now.

Diets are not wrong, but you still have to exercise. You can fast seven days and be down ten or fifteen pounds, but the Lord put self-preservation in your DNA: the body goes into saving, starts storing more water and more fat, and it comes back. You have to get out here and work out. You are not getting any younger, and your body is the temple: you must be fit to serve.

You do not hurt us; the Bible already said many are called but few are chosen, and that many shall depart from the faith.

precepts.text: A just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again.
precepts.point: Ham saw the nakedness of his father and did not cover him; Shem and Japheth went backward and covered their father without looking. The commandments concerning nakedness were being applied; Leviticus 18 opens those laws.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why: “For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.” Noah was a just man. He fell here, drinking of the wine until he was drunken, but a just man rises up again. One fall does not undo righteousness; Noah was still perfect and righteous in the eyes of the Most High.

precepts.text: If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength is small; the strength applied to the Bible is small.
precepts.point: Jacob knew there was corn in Egypt because Joseph had already told Pharaoh exactly what to do to save up in the time of tribulation; when Jacob heard, he sent out the fathers. Applying these attributes makes better men, women, brothers, and sisters, to bring forth the nation unto the kingdom of God.

note.label: Genesis 45: Joseph Made Known unto His Brethren

precepts.why:
“If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength is small.” If a man faints when the trial comes, the strength he applied to the Bible is small. Joseph did not faint: he endured Potiphar’s house and the prison, and came out governor over all the land of Egypt.

When the day of adversity comes, read the afflictions of the forefathers and the attributes they had in those times, and apply them. That is where the strength comes from.

precepts.text: If thou sayest, behold, we knew it not, doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? The excuse of ignorance does not stand before him.
precepts.point: Saying we knew it not does not stand before the Most High. Doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it, and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? A lot of people say they never heard this truth when they heard it and did not want to apply it. The Most High knows the things that come into your mind, every one of them; he created us and knows us better than we know ourselves, and he knows whether you sinned through ignorance or willfully.

note.label: Leviticus 4: The Sin Offering for Sins of Ignorance

precepts.why:
Saying we knew it not does not stand before the Most High. “If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?”

A lot of people say they never heard this truth when they heard it and did not want to apply it. Some of what is called ignorance is not ignorance; it is complacency, a lack of faith, a mind not in the spirit. He that pondereth the heart knows whether the ruler sinned through ignorance or willfully, and renders to every man according to his works.

precepts.text: Doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? He that keepeth thy soul knoweth whether the ignorance is real.
precepts.point: The scripture that pops up again is the same one: if thou sayest, behold, we knew it not, doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? Worldly family and coworkers that are not keeping the laws talk the same way, not understanding they condemn themselves because they are not repenting; that card cannot be pulled on the Messiah.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
Sin through ignorance in the holy things of the Lord, and the scripture that pops up again is the same one: “If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?”

He that keepeth thy soul knows whether the ignorance is real. Worldly family and coworkers that are not keeping the laws talk the same way, we knew it not, not understanding they condemn themselves because they are not repenting. That card cannot be pulled on the Messiah.

precepts.text: A just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again; under Christ there is room to repent and stand back up.
precepts.point: The daughter of any priest that profaned herself by playing the whore profaned her father and was burnt with fire. Under the law it was straight death, and we are all guilty of these things; this is why Christ had to come. Thank the Most High for the blood of Christ, that we can repent, correct ourselves, and keep moving, for a just man falleth and riseth up again.

note.label: Leviticus 21: The Holiness of the Priests, the Sons of Aaron

precepts.why:
The priests were held to an even higher standard, and “the daughter of any priest, if she profane herself by playing the whore, she profaneth her father: she shall be burnt with fire.” Under the law it was straight death, and we are all guilty of these things; this is why Christ had to come.

“For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.” Thank the Most High for the blood of Christ, that we can repent, correct ourselves, and keep moving. Under Christ there is room to fall, repent and stand back up.

precepts.text: This is really a precept for the just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again; the fall does not end your service to the Most High.
precepts.point: Fear not: ye have done all this wickedness, yet turn not aside from following the Lord, but serve the Lord with all your heart. Yes, you did all this wickedness, but now you get it; after all the wickedness you have done, still serve the Lord. That is heavy.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
Samuel does not tell Israel they did nothing wrong: “Fear not: ye have done all this wickedness: yet turn not aside from following the Lord, but serve the Lord with all your heart”. Yes, you did all this wickedness, but now you get it; after all the wickedness you have done, still serve the Lord. That is heavy.

This is really a precept for “a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.” The fall does not end your service to the Most High. The just man rises up again and keeps following the Lord with all his heart.

precepts.text: My son, fear thou the Lord and the king, and meddle not with them that are given to change; Saul was the king and put out an order, and when someone among you tries to change the orders of the king, do not meddle with him, because he will lead you into error, which is exactly what happened next.
precepts.point: Jonathan said, My father hath troubled the land: see how mine eyes have been enlightened, because I tasted a little of this honey; how much more, if haply the people had eaten freely of the spoil of their enemies, had there not been now a much greater slaughter among the Philistines? He began to convince the people that eating was the better idea and that the king's order was folly.

note.label: 1 Samuel 14: By Many or by Few

precepts.why:
Jonathan had not heard his father charge the people with the oath. He dipped the end of his rod in an honeycomb, “and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes were enlightened.” Like the first taste after a long fast, he felt like a whole new creature. Then he was told, “Thy father straitly charged the people with an oath, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth any food this day. And the people were faint.”

Jonathan answered, “My father hath troubled the land”, and began to convince the people that eating was the better idea and that the king’s order was folly: “How much more, if haply the people had eaten freely to day of the spoil of their enemies which they found? for had there not been now a much greater slaughter among the Philistines?”

“My son, fear thou the Lord and the king: and meddle not with them that are given to change”. Saul was the king and put out an order. When someone among you tries to change the orders of the king, do not meddle with him, because he will lead you into error, which is exactly what happened next.

precepts.text: A just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again.
precepts.point: Through David's judgment, Solomon was still able to be born; it was all part of the plan of the Most High. The backup master plan behind everything was Christ, who still had to be born through David's lineage; David was still loved and still forgiven, which shows repentance, and that even the mighty among us can fall and yet rise back up.

note.label: 2 Samuel 12: Nathan's Parable and the Judgment on David's House

precepts.why:
“For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.”

David fell, and he rose up again. He was judged, he repented, and the Lord still loved him and gave him Solomon, whom Nathan called Jedidiah because of the Lord. Even the mighty among us can fall and yet rise back up.

precepts.text: A just man falleth seven times and riseth up again; that is what David did after his fall.
precepts.point: The Lord rewarded David according to his righteousness and the cleanness of his hands, for he kept the ways of the Lord and did not wickedly depart from his God; all the Lord's judgments were before him and he did not depart from his statutes. He kept himself from his own iniquity, holding back his flesh; the one time it overtook him he was judged and got right back on track, for a righteous man falls and rises again.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again”. That is what David did after his fall.

David held back his flesh. The one time it overtook him he was judged, and he got right back on track, for a righteous man falls and rises again. So he could still sing, “Therefore the Lord hath recompensed me according to my righteousness; according to my cleanness in his eye sight.”

precepts.text: Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth, lest the Lord see it and turn his wrath away from him. That wrath then turns onto you, even if the enemy is one of your own people you have issues with.
precepts.point: Every nation outside the Israelites falls in this category, seeking the heart of the Israelites without cause.

note.label: Psalm 40: Patient Waiting, Obedience Over Sacrifice, and the Great Congregation

precepts.why:
David prays for his enemies to be “driven backward and put to shame”, but there is a line we cannot cross: “Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth: Lest the Lord see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.”

If you rejoice when the enemy falls, the Lord turns his wrath away from him, and that wrath then turns onto you. That holds even if the enemy is one of your own people you have issues with. Leave the shaming to the Lord, and do not be glad over it.

precepts.text: A just man falls seven times and rises up again, so a fall does not undo the righteous man.
precepts.point: Take no heed to all the words that are spoken, lest thou hear thy servant curse thee, for thine own heart knows that thou hast likewise cursed others.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 7: A Good Name and the House of Mourning

precepts.why:
“For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.” A fall does not undo the righteous man: he rises up again.

That is how to read “there is not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.” Verse 20 is one of those verses the Christians love to pull out, the same as the New Testament saying we all fall short and Proverbs saying a just man falls seven times. It does not excuse sin; it shows that no man is sinless. The just man falls and rises up again, while the wicked fall into mischief.

precepts.text: It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment, which is the kind of respect being denied.
precepts.point: Peter opens his mouth and says the Most High is no respecter of persons, but in every nation he that feareth him and worketh righteousness is accepted, and the word was sent unto the children of Israel. "No respecter of persons" does not mean nations are equal, because the Most High plainly had respect unto Israel and chose Israel above all people; it means he does not respect persons in judgment concerning his law, so whether a man sins outside the law or inside it he is judged.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment.”

That is the kind of respect being denied. The Most High does not respect persons in judgment concerning his law. Whether a man sins outside the law or inside it, he is judged. He chose Israel by nation, but he does not excuse a man in judgment because of who he is.

precepts.point: Proverbs 24:16 also applies: a just man falls seven times and rises up again.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.”

We who seek to be justified by Christ are still found sinners, but that does not make Christ the minister of sin. The just man falls and rises up again; he does not continue in sin, he gets up and keeps the law.

King David fell, Solomon fell, Samson fell. In this flesh you are susceptible to make mistakes.
The wicked falls into mischief, and that is a different man: put out, he keeps the sin going, says well they put me out, and regresses right back into the world.

Then you are on some YouTube page saying we are a cult and we are evil. For every last one of you who leaves and speaks evil there is a judgment, because you did not leave us, you left Christ.
